prompt: In Chrome DevTools' Performance tab, a recorded interaction shows a red-bordered block in the summary strip labeled as a Long Task. What does that specifically mean?
choices: The main thread was blocked by a single task for more than 50ms
A network request took longer than 500ms to resolve
The page failed to reach First Contentful Paint
A JavaScript exception was thrown during the recording

prompt: A sort comparator calls a function that itself loops over the full array to recompute a value for every comparison. What is the main consequence visible in a flame chart, and the standard fix?
choices: The comparator function appears thousands of times with high total time; fix it by precomputing each row's value once before sorting (decorate-sort-undecorate)
The comparator causes a memory leak; fix it by calling the garbage collector manually
The comparator triggers forced reflows; fix it by batching DOM reads and writes
The comparator blocks the GPU thread; fix it by moving the sort to a Web Worker only

prompt: In an Xcode Instruments Time Profiler trace of a laggy table view, the call tree shows `cellForRowAt` leading into `CGImageSourceCreateImageAtIndex` consuming a large share of main-thread samples. What is the correct fix?
choices: Decode the image on a background queue, cache the result, and dispatch back to the main thread only to assign it to the image view
Replace UITableView with a UICollectionView to get better default performance
Increase the table view's estimated row height so fewer cells are measured
Call setNeedsDisplay() on the cell after configuring it

prompt: Using Instruments Allocations with Generation A and Generation B snapshots, you push and pop a detail screen five times between the snapshots. Generation B shows the detail view controller's persistent count at 5 instead of 0. What does this indicate?
choices: Something outside the normal view lifecycle is holding a strong reference, preventing the view controller from deallocating
The app is using too much CPU during the push/pop animation
The view controller's view hierarchy is too deeply nested
The detail screen is leaking only because ARC is disabled for that file

prompt: A Swift view model starts a repeating Timer whose closure captures self strongly (directly and inside a nested network callback). The view model's owner is dismissed, but the view model never deallocates. What combination of changes actually fixes this?
choices: Capture self weakly in both closures with [weak self], and call timer.invalidate() in deinit so the timer stops once the view model is finally released
Capture self weakly in both closures with [weak self] only; invalidation is unnecessary because ARC handles it automatically
Mark the ProfileViewModel class as final and remove the Timer entirely
Call timer.invalidate() immediately after creating the timer

prompt: A loop reads card.offsetWidth and then writes card.style.height for each card, one card at a time. DevTools shows a repeated stack of purple Layout blocks each flagged as a forced reflow. Why does this happen, and what's the fix?
choices: Interleaving a DOM read after a DOM write forces a synchronous layout on every iteration; batch all the reads first, then all the writes
The loop is too slow because of JavaScript's garbage collector; fix it by using a for-loop instead of forEach
offsetWidth is deprecated and should be replaced with getBoundingClientRect for better performance
The CSS transition duration is too long; shortening it removes the Layout blocks

prompt: A webpack-bundle-analyzer treemap shows moment.js's locale directory taking up roughly 230 KB of a 310 KB vendor bundle, even though the app only ever renders dates in one locale. What's the most direct fix?
choices: Add a webpack.IgnorePlugin targeting moment's locale directory and explicitly import only the needed locale file
Switch the build target from 'web' to 'node' in webpack.config.js
Replace webpack with Metro to get automatic locale tree-shaking
Move the moment import into a Web Worker so it doesn't count toward bundle size

prompt: A React Native FlatList's renderItem does `onPress={() => onSelect(item.id)}` and `style={{ padding: 12 }}` inline, and ContactRow is wrapped in React.memo. Profiling shows every row re-rendering whenever the parent re-renders. Why does React.memo fail to prevent this?
choices: renderItem allocates a new function and a new object literal on every call, so React.memo's shallow prop comparison always sees different references and re-renders anyway
React.memo does not work with FlatList's renderItem prop under any circumstances
FlatList re-renders every row by design regardless of memoization to keep scroll position in sync
The keyExtractor is returning a new key on every render, forcing a full remount
